evidence: Partially-verified: Jira project-version READ is in production (acli_rest.py:199-208, GET /rest/api/3/project/{key}/versions), but no repo code calls POST /rest/api/3/version or DELETE /rest/api/3/version/{id}. The plan records a permissions check only, not an exercised create or delete.

findings.finding: Version create and delete are new Jira Cloud endpoint surfaces for this repo, and the plan names them without the details that make them work. POST /rest/api/3/version needs a body with `name` plus the project (Cloud documents `projectId`), which means first resolving REB's id. The created version's `id` must be read from the response, so `_direct_rest_post_json` has to be used, not `_direct_rest_post_raw`, which discards the body. DELETE /rest/api/3/version/{id} is documented as deprecated in Cloud in favour of POST /rest/api/3/version/{id}/removeAndSwap, and its behaviour when the version is still on an issue has not been observed. Also, the client's POST retry wrapper can re-send a create that already succeeded server-side, which returns a duplicate-name 400 and leaves the test without the version id.

If the passes run in the CI checkout, or in any repo with other tickets or bindings, every pass writes into that store: prev_snapshot, bridge state, BRIDGE_ALERT events and inbound edits. The filter then only guards Jira dispatch, not the local side.

findings.finding: The plan deletes versions with `DELETE /rest/api/3/version/{id}`, which Atlassian's Jira Cloud v3 docs mark as deprecated. The recommended replacement is `POST /rest/api/3/version/{id}/removeAndSwap`. The same deprecated call is planned in three places: each test's finally block, the conftest backstop and the workflow's curl cleanup. If Atlassian removes the endpoint, all three cleanup layers fail together and run-scoped versions pile up in the shared REB project. Jira DC 10 has already removed the equivalent v2 DELETE.

findings.finding: The new summary-based issue sweep (conftest backstop and workflow cleanup) depends on Jira Cloud JQL text search (`summary ~ ...`) matching a hyphenated token such as `cloudprobe-<run_id>`. This behaviour is unverified. In Jira text search `-` is a reserved character and the analyzer splits on hyphens, so the query may match too little (the leak goes unswept) or too much (it also matches `cloudprobe` issues from other runs). The sweep deletes what it finds, so an over-match would delete a concurrent probe's issues in the shared REB project.
findings.location: Implementation notes > Binding ('the conftest backstop and the workflow cleanup also delete REB issues whose summary contains the run prefix')
scenarios: Two probe runs overlap. Run A's backstop runs `summary ~ "cloudprobe-111"`, Lucene tokenizes it into `cloudprobe` plus `111` (or reads the hyphen as an exclusion), and the hits include run B's in-flight issue, which gets deleted mid-test.
Locally the prefix is `cloudprobe-local-<hex>`, and the JQL misses the issue created by the bind pass, so a crash between bind and labelling leaks it.
findings.suggested_fix: In both the conftest backstop and the workflow step, treat `project = REB AND summary ~ "<prefix>"` as a candidate filter only. Delete a hit only if `<prefix> in hit.fields.summary`, compared as an exact substring in Python or jq. Consider also putting the bare run_id (no hyphens) in the summary so the JQL term matches reliably.
